title: Build a month's email send calendar under a frequency cap
prompt:
Marrowfield Garden Co. sells seeds, tools and houseplants online and emails its subscribers. Its CRM lead wants February's email calendar built from the supplied campaign plan and subscriber export, following the supplied calendar policy exactly.

Deliver one file in your reply, under a line with its file name, as CSV with exactly the header shown: one row per campaign, no totals row, and nothing inside the file but its rows.

### schedule.csv
campaign_id,send_date,audience_size,reason
Every campaign in the plan, once. `send_date` is the date the campaign goes out, as YYYY-MM-DD, or `none` when the policy does not send it. `audience_size` is how many subscribers the campaign goes to under the policy, given also for a campaign that is not sent. `reason` is empty for a campaign sent on its requested date; for every other campaign it is the policy's reason code.

End your reply with this answer block, one line per answer: the label, a colon and the number alone. If you use a thousands separator, use a comma.

A1: <number of campaigns sent on a date other than their requested date>
A2: <number of campaigns not sent>
A3: <total emails sent in February: the audience sizes of the campaigns that are sent, added up>
A4: <the most emails any one subscriber receives in February>
A5: <number of subscribers who receive that many>

This is a plan for review. Schedule nothing in any email platform and fetch nothing external.

completion.check: schedule.csv is in the reply, under a line with its file name.

Every one of the plan's 12 campaigns appears exactly once in schedule.csv, no campaign appears that is not in the plan, and every send_date is a date written as YYYY-MM-DD or the word none. Full credit for no error; zero credit at 1.
The reply ends with the answer block and all 5 labeled answers A1-A5 are present, each on its own line with the number alone.
A1 states how many campaigns the policy sends on a date other than their requested date. Full credit for the exact figure; zero credit 1 or more off.
A2 states how many campaigns the policy does not send. Full credit for the exact figure; zero credit 1 or more off.
A3 states the total emails sent in February: the audience sizes of the campaigns the policy sends, added up. Full credit for the exact figure; zero credit 20 or more off.
A4 states the most emails any one subscriber receives in February on the policy's calendar. Full credit for the exact figure; zero credit 1 or more off.
A5 states how many subscribers receive that many emails. Full credit for the exact figure; zero credit 3 or more off.

skill_adherence.check: Every campaign has the send date the policy's procedure gives it, or none where the procedure does not send it. Full credit for none wrong or missing; zero credit at 2 or more.

Every campaign that does not go out on its requested date carries the code of the first rule that rules out that date, and every other campaign has no reason. Full credit for none wrong or missing; zero credit at 2 or more.
Every campaign's audience_size is the number of active subscribers in at least one of its segments, each counted once. Full credit for none wrong or missing; zero credit at 2 or more.

best_practices.check: The reply states no figure about Marrowfield's subscribers or campaigns (an open rate, a click rate, revenue, a list size) that the supplied files do not contain or yield. A clearly labelled assumption is not data.
